description.narrative: Skills Development is vital to securing and promoting decent work, particularly for India’s ability to leverage the potential demographic dividend. The CPO builds on achievements and partnerships established in the previous biennium to provide technical guidance in key areas to the constituents. Anchored in ILO’s Quality Apprenticeships Recommendations, 2023 (No. 208), ILO facilitated high-level policy dialogue and capacity-building workshops for tripartite constituents through South-South and Triangular Cooperation (SSTC) project. Under Apprenticeship Development for Universal Lifelong Learning and Training (ADULT) project, ILO developed India Country Report. Complimenting this, a dedicated study was conducted to propose policy advice aimed at enhancing apprenticeships in MSMEs in India. In collaboration with UNICEF/YuWaah, ILO organized Skills Innovation Challenge Call, which piloted four projects that focused on upgrading informal apprenticeships through digital transformation. Building on these outcomes and leveraging newly adopted recommendation, the CPO is advancing policy recommendations, based on good practices and lessons learned from Skills Innovation Challenge Call. The ILO continues to engage in high-level consultations and policy dialogues with national constituents on Quality Apprenticeships. These platforms foster exchange of insights and co-creation of strategies to strengthen inclusivity, relevance and effectiveness of apprenticeship. The ILO led development of South Asia Qualifications Referencing Framework (SAQRF) under joint ILO-IOM-UN Women regional programme. The CPO tries to support endorsement of SAQRF and referencing of National Skills Qualifications Framework to the SAQRF. Additionally, ILO is contributing technical inputs to draft of National Policy for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship 2025 and serves as a member of committee constituted by the government tasked to make recommendations on the criteria for categorizing workers.
